news.title: Falconets cry for help after Poland denies visas to 15 Nigeria U-20 players
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Find it fast with our new search feature at Legit.ng! Nigeria's preparations for the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup have been thrown into chaos after Poland refused to grant visas to 15 players in the Falconets' final squad, leaving the team in a desperate situation weeks before the tournament begins. A team official described the crisis as a "big, hot mess," questioning how the side could possibly compete at a World Cup with only 15 players cleared for travel. A post by veteran Nigerian journalist Oluwashina Okeleji on X, confirmed the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) and head coach Moses Aduku are now working urgently to resolve the visa issue and get the remaining players on the flight to Europe.

(Photo by Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images) The group critical against Gianni Infantino includes legends like Claudio Pizarro, Juan Sebastian Veron, Emmanuel Adebayor, Didier Drogba and David James. A coalition of former internationals — among them World Cup winners and FIFA Legends — has demanded urgent reforms at FIFA, accusing the organisation’s leadership under President Gianni Infantino of being intoxicated by power.

news.title: The Blue Tigers' World Cup Test: What fixtures against Brazil, Panama and New Zealand mean for India
news.lede: For Indian football, 2026 could become a year defined not by qualification for the FIFA World Cup, but by the opportunity to measure itself against some of the teams that will take part in it. India are set to face an unprecedented run of opposition from the World Cup this year, with a friendly against Panama expected in September, a historic meeting with Brazil scheduled for October 3 in Kolkata and two away fixtures against New Zealand in November. There is even the possibility of another World Cup opponent being added to the October international window. That could give India four, and potentially five, opportunities to test themselves against teams that have reached the game's biggest stage.

news.title: Mikel Obi calls for radical overhaul of Nigerian football, demands NFF board resignation
news.lede: Former Super Eagles captain John Obi Mikel has called for sweeping reforms in Nigerian football, urging changes in the leadership and administration of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) amid growing concerns over the direction of the game. Mikel’s statement comes as Nigerian football faces a sustained decline, with the Super Eagles missing the 2026 FIFA World Cup after failing to qualify for the previous edition in Qatar. Read Also: Mikel Obi: Disband NFF if Nigeria misses 2026 World Cup. The former Chelsea midfielder said the country cannot afford another failure to book the World Cup and called for the appointment of capable administrators who can rebuild the football system.

news.title: Rodri capture can catapult Barcelona back to very top of European game: GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer window
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: World Cup winners, Fifa legends say Infantino blinded by power
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been under mounting pressure to resign after shelving his now-abandoned proposal to create a commercial body for Fifa tournament rights and sell a 20% stake to private investors. (EPA Images pic) GENEVA: A group of former international players, including World Cup winners and Fifa legends, called on Monday for immediate change at world football's governing body, saying its leadership under embattled president Gianni Infantino had been blinded by power. Infantino has been under mounting pressure to resign after shelving his now-abandoned proposal to create a commercial body for Fifa tournament rights and sell off 20% to private investors.

news.title: Maradona 'Hand of God' football sells for $3.35m at auction
news.lede: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his 'Hand of God' goal against England at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for $3.35m (€2.9m). The sale price achieved by Heritage Auctions in the United States was approximately $6.7m (€5.7m) below the $10m (€8.6m) estimate. The Dallas-based auction house had placed a $2.5m (€2.1m) starting price on the Adidas Azteca ball. Maradona scored twice in Argentina’s quarter-final victory over England on 22 June, 1986 at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

news.title: Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ football sold at auction
news.lede: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his ‘Hand of God’ goal against England at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for 3.35million US dollars (£2.45m). The sale price achieved by Heritage Auctions in the United States was approximately 6.7m USD (£4.9m) below the 10m USD (£7.3m) estimate. The Dallas-based auction house had placed a 2.5m USD (£1.8m) starting price on the Adidas Azteca ball. Maradona scored twice in Argentina’s quarter-final victory over England on June 22, 1986 at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.
